A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CBS research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite the expanded theory and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original CBS experiments, including mathematical reasoning scores, training times, ablations, buffer sensitivity, and rollout case studies.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the original benchmark, efficiency, ablation, and supplementary analysis results. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The rollout representations, MLP scheduler, selection rules, reward augmentation, replay buffer, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The new affine reward normalization belongs to the theoretical analysis, not a reported implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions train on the same DAPO/MATH mixture and evaluate mathematical reasoning on AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, MATH500, Minerva, and Olympiad. No evaluated domain or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same base-model, GRPO, DAPO, and GSPO comparisons with CBS and CBS*. The ablation comparisons retain Random, w/o EMA, and w/o Entropy. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6.1, Appendix D, and Table 4 retain the same model sizes, training budgets, rollout settings, checkpoint selection, and Avg@4/Avg@32 evaluation. The exploration schedule introduced in the proof is not a reported experimental setting change.

E4.justification: The scheduler, EMA, and entropy ablations, buffer-size sweep, feature-score correlations, training dynamics, and filtered/selected rollout case studies are retained. Appendix figure renumbering does not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports new training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. Evaluation sampling averages remain unchanged; revisions to theoretical probability statements belong to T1.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 preserve their numerical results, including the 43.93 average for Qwen3-4B DAPO + CBS. The original experimental plots, sensitivity findings, and qualitative case studies also match after renumbering.

T1.justification: Section 5 replaces the next-round-performance, purely greedy analysis with a normalized gain-reward formulation that includes exploration. Theorem 5.4 changes from a direct regret bound to an expected-regret bound with probability over scheduler initialization. Appendix B substantially replaces the regression argument, adds a uniform perturbation lemma, and develops auxiliary-trajectory, exploration-cost, and revised network-width conditions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified intra-group selection and global reuse, theoretical regret support, and improved reasoning performance and training efficiency. The formal guarantee is revised without rewriting these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly describes the regret bound as data-dependent and explains that favorable low-dimensional NTK structure can keep its effective dimension bounded. Empirical interpretations and existing limitations, including deterioration with excessively large buffers, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Table 4 retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, prompt template, reward verification, and evaluation instructions. The formerly linked repository is now printed explicitly, but both links identify the same code repository.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a short background paragraph citing additional graph, multi-agent, and LLM research, while two bandit references are removed. The main related-work discussion and CBS's positioning against heuristic rollout selection remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and notation corrections, updates author affiliations and publication information, adds acknowledgements, and introduces Appendix A subsections. Theoretical explanations expand, but the overall narrative and most prose remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds an explanatory RLVR pipeline diagram as Figure 5 in Appendix A and relocates several existing main-text displays. Original appendix Figures 5–12 become Figures 6–13 with their experimental content preserved; the overall visual style remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves theoretical transparency by explicitly normalizing the gain reward, accounting for exploration, and specifying an expected-regret guarantee in Section 5 and Appendix B. The new pipeline illustration also improves exposition. These are limited gains: the guarantee remains idealized and requires a special exploration schedule, so the revision should not be read as establishing a stronger guarantee for the unchanged experimental implementation.
